events.title: Breathing & Meditation: The Natural Path to Better Immunity and Restful Sleep
events.description: Experience the soothing calm of meditation presented by library partner, Art of Living Foundation. Enjoy this free, one-hour session focused on managing stress and anxiety through simple, evidence-based techniques. These sessions are open to all adults and includes optional light physical movement, breathing practices, and guided meditation. No prior experience is necessary. Typical agenda for this one hour as followed: Optional Yoga Stretches (10 minutes) Light, beginner-friendly stretches Will be offered based on participant interest Breathing Techniques (10 minutes) Guided practice of calming breathwork Techniques that can be used daily to reduce stress Guided Meditation (20 minutes) Deep relaxation and mindfulness practice Designed to calm the mind and promote inner peace Experience Sharing & Program Info (10 minutes) Participants may share experiences Information about the Art of Living and wellness programs Optional: 3-minute video clip of past participant testimonials (if AV available) This program is geared to enrich the lives of adults and seniors. Registration is online.
events.blurb: Learn simple breathing and meditation techniques to ease stress and sleep better in this hour-long library session.

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club - Hillview
events.description: Join us to practice, build, and strengthen your English-speaking skills. This is a fun, welcoming and respectful environment for adult English learners. Club meetings are held weekly and led online by a trained facilitator. Our dedicated and experienced volunteer, Patricia, leads the program and will help you build confidence in your English-speaking abilities. Please be sure to register by clicking the Register button. By providing your email address, you will receive the Zoom meeting link before the program begins.

events.title: Amplify: Coco: Intro to Coding
events.description: Ever wanted to build your own video game or animation, With your friends, at the same time? Join us for a coding workshop to try Coco. Build, where you snap blocks together like puzzle pieces to create games, art, and more in real time! No experience needed, just bring your imagination. Let's build something awesome together! Grades 3-6. Library computers will be provided- you do not need to bring a laptop or other device to participate. This program is part of Amplify: Teen Voices, where teens who are passionate about a topic are mentored through the process of leading a library program.

events.title: 1-on-1 Tech Help | Trợ Giúp Kỹ Năng Máy Tính Bằng Tiếng Việt
events.description: This event offered in Vietnamese. Are you or your loved ones struggling with using a smartphone, downloading apps, or making video calls to see the family? Come join our Free One-on-One Tech Mentor Support sessions. We can help you with: Basic help for smartphones, tablets, and computers Downloading and using everyday apps Making video calls (Zoom, FaceTime, Google Meet) to stay connected Exploring AI tools and answering your AI questions/concerns Navigating our library website and wonderful digital resources Note: Our support is focused on basic technology questions. events.title: Banned Book Week Trivia
events.description: Registration is required and seats are limited. This event is intended for ages 15 and up only. What do you know about banned books or Banned Book Week in general? Join us to test your knowledge on all things banned book related! In teams of 5, you will work together to answer 40 questions from 4 related categories. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Team up in groups of five to test your knowledge of banned books at this library trivia session.

events.title: The Financial Side of Estate Planning: Beyond Wills and Trusts
events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. Most people think of estate planning as a legal task — a will, a trust, a folder in a drawer. But many of the decisions that determine how your assets actually reach your family are financial ones, made on account forms and beneficiary designations years apart. What you'll learn: What legal documents do... And don't. Wills, trusts, powers of attorney, and healthcare directives: what each one accomplishes, and where its authority stops. How your assets actually transfer. Why beneficiary designations and account titling often decide who receives what - no matter what your will says. Overlooked areas that cause issues. Outdated beneficiaries, joint ownership problems, blended families, digital footprints, overlooked retirement rules and uncoordinated advice. Taxes, family, and legacy goals. How inherited retirement accounts are taxed, and how to coordinate family, charitable, and legal decisions into a cohesive plan. Every attendee receives complimentary resources, including an Estate Planning Readiness Checklist to organize their own information. Who should attend: Retirees Those approaching retirement Parents and grandparents Anyone who has accumulated assets and wants to protect their family We are also hosting the same workshop on Thursday, October 8 at 2:00 p.m. Presented by Daniel L. Foss, Ch FC, CLU.
events.blurb: Hear a talk on the financial decisions behind estate planning, beyond just wills and trusts.

events.title: The Messenger of Peace: Japanese Crane Textile Sculpture
events.description: Registration is required. Seats and materials are limited. Please only register if you plan on attending. Join sustainable artist and educator Leila Ghasempor for a hands-on art workshop exploring the beauty, history, and symbolism of the Japanese crane. Traditionally associated with hope, longevity, and peace. Participants will learn about the cultural meaning of the crane while exploring textile construction, sculptural form, and geometric folding techniques to create their own three-dimensional fabric crane. No sewing experience is required. All materials will be provided. This class is intended for ages 18 and up only. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Make a Japanese crane textile sculpture while learning the bird's history and symbolism with artist Leila Ghasempor.

events.title: Planning Your Cool Vegetable Garden in Our Mediterranean Climate
events.description: Seating is limited. Registration is recommended. Walk-ins are also welcome. Did you know that we can grow cool season vegetables in Santa Clara County? It's true! With our cool (but not cold) rainy season we can grow all sorts of vegetables like greens such as lettuce, chard and kale, to cruciferous vegetables like broccoli or cauliflower to root vegetables like beets, carrots and radishes. Come learn what you can grow with Matt Hall, UC Master Gardener. He will go over the basics such as soil, water and fertilizing requirements, and show all of the different plants that do great here. Infrared assistive listening systems are available for use during this event. Please see Library staff for assistance.
events.blurb: Learn which cool-season vegetables grow well in Santa Clara County's Mediterranean climate.

events.description: Love the idea of a book club but don't have time for a whole novel? Join our Short Story Social, a relaxed "book club" for short-story fans and busy readers. events.description: Step into the world of a mysterious mansion where one fateful evening takes a deadly turn. You'll be given a character to play, complete with secrets, suspicions, and motives of your own. As the story unfolds, clues will be revealed and everyone becomes a suspect. Work with your fellow guests to uncover hidden secrets, piece together the evidence, and determine who committed the murder before the mystery is solved. Will you crack the case, or will the murderer get away with it? No acting experience is necessary—just bring your imagination and your detective skills! Whether you're a seasoned sleuth or simply looking for a fun and theatrical evening, everyone has a role to play in this interactive murder mystery. Registration required and TBD
events.blurb: Take on a character with hidden motives and work with fellow guests to solve a mansion murder mystery.

events.title: Afghan Cassette Archive: Stories, Sounds, and Music from Afghanistan
events.description: Registration is recommended. Walk-ins are also welcome. Join Omid Jahan, founder of the Afghan Cassette Archive (@afghancassettearchive), for a multimedia listening session exploring Afghanistan's rich musical history through rare cassette recordings, archival materials, and personal stories. The program will highlight Afghan music from different eras and communities, including recordings preserved from Afghanistan and the Afghan diaspora. Attendees will have the opportunity to hear selections from the archive, learn about the stories behind the music and artists, and view original cassette tapes and other archival materials. The session offers a unique look at Afghan history, culture, migration, and memory through the music that has traveled across generations. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Hear rare cassette recordings and stories from the Afghan Cassette Archive's founder Omid Jahan.

events.title: Seed Packets Demystified
events.description: Seating is limited. Registration is recommended. Walk-ins are also welcome. Do you love to look at seed catalogs and seed packets but wonder if you'd really be able to grow plants from seeds? Do you stare at the seed rack in your local nursery puzzling through what variety to plant and when you should plant it? Most seed packets contain a wealth of information to help you plant seeds of the right plant in the right place at the right time. But many of us don't bother reading the fine print, and jump straight to the planting. Join us for a lively discussion and analysis of how reading the fine print on your seed packets can help you be more successful in your garden. Infrared assistive listening systems are available for use during this event. Please see Library staff for assistance.
events.blurb: Learn how to read seed packets and catalogs so you can actually pick and grow the right varieties.

events.title: Wild Fungi of California
events.description: Join Carrie Staller from Fork in the Path for an interactive hour of hands-on fun exploring the fascinating world of mushrooms! Learn how to identify mushrooms, discover chanterelles, morels, and porcini, and understand the difference between edible and poisonous varieties. We will have some specimens to touch and smell. This program is perfect for curious minds of all ages eager to learn about the natural world. About Fork in the Path: Fork in the Path offers forest-to-ocean-to-table learning programs for the adventurous of all ages across Northern California. We believe learning to forage and eating seasonal wild food is transformational. It helps us become more connected, whole, healthy, and happy. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Hear Carrie Staller explain how to identify mushrooms and tell edible species from poisonous ones.

events.title: Informed Community Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for the Informed Community Book Club, a space dedicated to exploring and discussing pertinent social, economic, and political issues. If you are interested in participating in our democratic institutions or just making friends, join us! September's book will be All-American Nativism: How the Bipartisan War on Immigrants Explains Politics as We Know It, by Daniel Denvir From the publisher's website: It is often said that with the election of Donald Trump nativism was raised from the dead. After all, here was a president who organized his campaign around a rhetoric of unvarnished racism and xenophobia. Among his first acts on taking office was to block foreign nationals from seven predominantly Muslim countries from entering the United States. But although his actions may often seem unprecedented, they are not as unusual as many people believe. This story doesn't begin with Trump. For decades, Republicans and Democrats alike have employed xenophobic ideas and policies, declaring time and again that "illegal immigration" is a threat to the nation's security, wellbeing, and future. The profound forces of all-American nativism have, in fact, been pushing politics so far to the right over the last forty years that, for many people, Trump began to look reasonable. As Daniel Denvir argues, issues as diverse as austerity economics, free trade, mass incarceration, the drug war, the contours of the post 9/11 security state, and, yes, Donald Trump and the Alt-Right movement are united by the ideology of nativism, which binds together assorted anxieties and concerns into a ruthless political project. All-American Nativism provides a powerful and impressively researched account of the long but often forgotten history that gave us Donald Trump. The discussion will be hosted by former Los Gatos Planning Commissioner and current president of the Los Gatos Anti-Racism Coalition Jeff Suzuki.
events.blurb: Discuss social, economic, and political issues around this month's featured nonfiction pick.

events.title: Nature Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Nature lovers and science enthusiasts, we invite you to be part of our Nature Book Club! Every two months, we'll explore nonfiction books about nature and science, and compare notes in a friendly, welcoming discussion. August's book is The Wild Dark, by Craig Childs. About The Wild Dark: At a time when most people on Earth live in regions of acute light pollution, Craig Childs takes us on a journey to rediscover the awesome power of night itself. Seeking not the absence of light, but the presence of the universe, master storyteller Craig Childs sets out to bike from the blinding lights of the Las Vegas Strip to one of the darkest spots in North America. A fearless explorer of both the natural world and the human imagination, Childs guides us on a quest to rediscover the heavens and to ask: "What does it do to us to not see the night sky?" The Wild Dark is at once an adventure story, a field guide, and a celebration of the awesome power of night itself, inviting us to look up and to look inward, eyes wide and sparkling with stars. Craig Childs has published more than a dozen critically acclaimed books, including The Secret Knowledge of Water, Atlas of a Lost World, Virga & Bone, and Tracing Time. Many of his books have won awards including Reading the West Book Award, Southwest Book of the Year, Foreword Indies medalist, the Orion Book Award, and more. Childs lives in southwest Colorado.
events.blurb: Discuss a nonfiction nature or science book with fellow nature lovers in the group.

events.title: Cookbook Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: October's theme is "cake or pie"! Each month we have a theme that you are free to interpret however you'd like. Choose a recipe to make from one of the many cookbooks or other resources in our collection- don't worry, we'll have plenty of suggestions for you! Then we'll meet to talk about books and cooking and enjoy each other's company. Photos of your finished dish are encouraged but not required. Are you Team Cake or Team Pie? Both? This month we'll be showing our team spirit by making either a cake or a pie, depending on which team you're on. You can make it sweet or savory, big enough for a crowd or small enough to be held in your hand- it's up to you! Think a Swedish smrgstrta or a savory hand pie, or one of the many, many cupcake recipes available. Or if you really are Team Both, you might consider attempting the legendary cherpumple! Browse our incredible cookbook collection in the Library or our ebooks on Cloud Library or The Palace Project, find something that looks interesting to you, and cook! Come to our meeting ready to talk all about what you made and the book you used.

events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for the Informed Community Book Club, a space dedicated to exploring and discussing pertinent social, economic, and political issues. If you are interested in participating in our democratic institutions or just making friends, join us! November's book will be The Corporate Sabotage of America's Future and What We Can Do About It, by Robert Weissman From the publisher's website: Long-time corporate accountability crusaders Robert Weissman, Public Citizen president, and Joan Claybrook, Public Citizen president emeritus, investigate how giant corporations corrupt the policy-making process to block reforms favored by overwhelming majorities of the American people, and to enrich themselves through far-reaching corporate welfare schemes. The Corporate Sabotage of America's Future And What We Can Do About It pulls back the curtain on the hidden tactics that big corporations employ to have their way in Washington, D.C. and state capitols and city halls across the nation. The discussion will be hosted by former Los Gatos Planning Commissioner and current president of the Los Gatos Anti-Racism Coalition Jeff Suzuki.
events.blurb: Discuss The Corporation and other pressing social, economic, and political issues with fellow book club members.

events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: The Los Gatos Library has partnered with @Girls Who Code to create a club meant for people ages 12-18 to learn to code and change the world! "What will I learn? events.title: Sound Bath Healing Meditation
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Gaby Castro-Moroder is Back for another Sound Healing session! Come join us! Sound and music is used as a method of healing across various mediums. After being told for years that she has a healing presence, Gaby Castro started her sound healing journey and took certification courses in tuning forks, crystal sound bowls, and Tibetan sound bowls. Now she provides sound healing group and individual sessions under the name Song Pine and Stone, bringing her gentle presence to those in need. A group sound healing session runs about 60-90 minutes and includes the use of crystal sound healing bowls, Tibetan bowls, tuning forks, and various other sound healing instruments. Attendees will bring their own yoga mats, blankets, pillows, and whatever else they need to be comfortable during the session. Instruments will be played to create a sound bath and attendees will be encouraged to relax and enjoy the soft, soothing sounds. When the session ends, attendees will be asked to rehydrate and we'll discuss how the session felt for everyone. Age Range: Adults and Seniors Note: A consent form may be required and provided at the event. Attendees need to consult with their physician and get approval to attend healing sessions if they have metal in their bodies, suffered concussions, have a pacemaker, use an insulin pump, and the like. If in doubt, consult your physician before the session. The Los Gatos Library recognizes the diversity of our community and is committed to accessibility for all patrons. We strive to make every visitor feel comfortable by ensuring equal access to programs, services, and activities. If you require a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in a library program, please contact library@losgatosca.gov
events.blurb: Lie back and let Gaby Castro-Moroder's sound healing session wash over you with instruments used for relaxation.

events.title: Cookbook Swap
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Do you have cookbooks that you never use sitting around? Or are you looking to add some new books to your collection? Come to our cookbook swap and meet some fellow cookbook enthusiasts, learn about our Cookbook Club, and maybe get a new book or two while finding a new home for ones you don't use anymore. This will be our very first Cookbook Swap, and if everyone has a good time, we can look into making it a regular event. For now, we will only limit the number of books you can bring to what you can carry yourself and we ask that the books you bring are reasonably clean and in good condition. If you'd like, we'll have note cards for you to mark your favorite recipes in the books so their new owners will have a fun place to start.
events.blurb: Bring cookbooks to trade, meet fellow cooks, and pick up new titles at the swap.

events.blurb: Bring your needlework or textile project and stitch alongside other crafters of every skill level.

events.title: Monday Morning Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for a discussion of Milkman, by Anna Burns Winner of the Man Booker Prize. A young woman navigates romance, politics, and social judgment in Ireland during the "Troubles." "Everything about this novel rings true…original, funny, disarmingly oblique and unique: different." - The Guardian. The Monday Morning book club meets in the Library Conference Room, and new members are welcome at any time.

events.description: Early learners (babies and toddlers) and their families are welcome to join us at the Library for Storytime, where we will wiggle, sing, read, and dance together! events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Register to join in on this artistic and heroic exploration of bugs with Dr. Stephanie Dole, also known as Beetlelady! This class is for ages 6-12, and registration is required (registration opens 3 weeks prior to the event).

events.title: Free Repairs with Repair Café
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Do you need help repairing something? Repair Café Silicon Valley will be at the library offering free repairs on household items such as toasters, lamps, radios, clothing, bikes, and more. Limit two items per household, last repairs accepted at 2:30 PM. Visit repaircafesv.org for more information about their mission and to see when other events are scheduled.

events.title: Monday Morning Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for a discussion of Felicia's Journey by William Trevor. A story of lost opportunities, naivety, and misplaced hopes of an Irish girl who leaves Ireland to find her boyfriend in England. By one of Ireland's most admired writers. The Monday Morning book club meets in the Library Conference Room, and new members are welcome at any time.
events.blurb: Discuss Felicia's Journey, William Trevor's story of an Irish girl chasing lost hopes in England, with the group.

events.title: Author Talk in Person - Interview with Past and Present Town Poets Laureate
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Come join us for a fun time as the Town's current Poet Laureate William Butler interviews our past Poet Laureate, Jen Siraganian, in celebration of her book Everything Has Been Moved, Even the Dead which won the 2026 Perugia Press Prize. Jen will read poems from the book and William will pose questions and facilitate discussion.
events.blurb: Hear Poet Laureate William Butler interview past laureate Jen Siraganian and listen to her read from her prize-winning book.

events.title: Job Interview Coaching for Adults & Teens

events.description: You applied for a job and received a call back for an interview. Congratulations! Do you want help preparing for the interview? Meet one-on-one with Daniel, an experienced job interview coach to help you prepare by giving feedback on your resume and conducting a mock interview. Sessions are one hour in length. Be prepared to share things with Daniel such as a current resume, the job position description you applied for, and if you can, come dressed as if you were going in to the actual interview. You must register for this event and registration ends the Thursday before the program. If you registered successfully, you will get a registration confirmation email with a link to pick your choice of time for this Saturday's program. Each session is one hour (15-30 minutes for interviewing + 30-45 minutes for helpful feedback). The one hour time slots to pick from are as follows: 10:00 - 11:00 am or 11:00 am - 12:00 pm. Please note that there is a 5 minute buffer to include any set up and help prevent any overlap between appointments. Resumes and job position descriptions are reviewed in advance. Please email documents to Jeff.Tibayan@sjlibrary.org by 5 PM on the Thursday before your Saturday session. This gives Daniel enough time to prepare job interview materials. events.title: Bay Area Comics and Comix Exhibition
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: The California Room's exhibit "Bay Area Comics and Comix" presents the history of American comic books, highlighting the participation of the San Francisco Bay Area. The exhibit displays comic books and materials illustrating our journey from 1842's The Adventures of Obadiah Oldbuck to the arrival of the modern comic book in the 1930s, and from there to a backlash against comics in the 1950s which resulted in comic book regulation. Continuing into the 1960's, the exhibit presents the explosion of "underground" comics which were largely a Bay Area phenomenon that opened the door to the emergence of the modern graphic novel and alternative comics. Kickoff Event Join us on Saturday June 6th for the Comix and Comics Exhibition Kickoff Event! Additional Information Parking available in the SJ Park Fourth Street Garage. First 90 minutes free.
events.blurb: Browse comic books and archival materials tracing Bay Area contributions to American comic history.

For the best experience we recommend bringing your own mobile device, but you can also follow the demonstration on the projector screen and take notes. 2026 Topics: Jan 24th - Library apps for reading e Books - an overview of SJPL's e-books collections from the library website with a focus on Libby/Overdrive - How to adjust reading settings like text size and lighting, and how to use the audiobook controls. If time allows, another app - Hoopla will be covered. Feb 28th - Using Zoom for Meetings and Social Connection - How to join meetings confidently or host simple meetings. Use of controls like muting and un-muting audio or video, how to see and use the chat function. Troubleshooting basics will also be covered. Mar 28th - Using Chat GPT - How to use Chat GPT to summarize long documents, organize items like receipts, ask effective questions and protect your privacy. Using Chat GPT responsibly will also be covered. April 25th - Managing contacts effectively and setting reminders - Add and organize contacts on your device. Create groups (family, emergency). Backup and sync safely. Set recurring reminders for daily tasks. Integrate reminders with calendars. May 23rd - Demystifying Ai June 27th - Spotting Ai Scams and Fake Messages July 25th - Emergency Features on Smartphones August 22nd - Google Translate for Travel and Communication - Use text, voice, and camera translation. Save common phrases for travel. Practice offline translation. September 26th - Using Chat GPT - How to use Chat GPT to summarize long documents, organize items like receipts, ask effective questions and protect your privacy. Using Chat GPT responsibly will also be covered. October 24th - How to Make Your Phone Easier to See - Adjusting text size, using the magnifier, voice to text, and dark mode. November 28th - Using Siri or Google Assistant - How to activate and use voice assistants Siri or Google Assistant. Practice common commands (weather, timers, calls). Manage privacy settings and shortcuts. (no program in December) Free. Class limited to 10 attendees. Registration Recommended. Walk-Ins welcome if space is available.

events.title: Fandom Swap
events.description: Did the fandom that used to be your absolute fave stop sparking joy for you? Have you hopped multiple fandoms over the years? Are your old acrylic standees, figurines, keychain charms, pins, prints, or stickers taking up too much space for the things from your new fandoms? Did you just clean out your room and ended up with massive piles of non-recyclable fandom merch you no longer want? Cambrian Branch Library has got you covered with Fandom Swap! We meet on the last Sunday of every month from 2 to 4 PM. Come bring in your clean, gently-loved fandom merchandise to find them new homes and keep them out of landfills! There's no need to stay for the full duration of this program either. Feel free to come by and drop off your stuff and leave, or if you'd like, you can stick around and see what other people bring in! So come join us to clean out your fandom goodies, meet fellow fans, or discover new fandoms! Official and unofficial merch are welcome, but all materials must be rated PG-13 and under. Selling is prohibited in this program.

events.title: Teen Writer's Circle
events.description: Join us for another session of the Teen Writer's Circle! Share your work, receive feedback, and connect with fellow teen writers in a supportive environment. We host interactive activities, engaging discussions, and peer feedback sessions to help each other grow. Our group is always evolving, and we'd love to hear your ideas to make it even better! Connect with fellow teen writers across the South Bay, share your stories, and find inspiration in a supportive community. Whether you're new to writing or have been writing for years, all levels are welcome! Register to receive an email reminder, but feel free to drop-in without registering.
events.blurb: Share your writing, get peer feedback, and connect with other teen writers in the circle.

events.title: Tai Chi with Nelson Ng
events.description: Join us for Tai Chi sessions with Nelson Ng! In this weekly class, participants will learn the basic principles and the philosophy behind Tai Chi, gaining flexibility and a better sense of balance through slow, gentle movement. Nelson started learning Chen's Tai Chi in 1989 from Master Gene Chen, who was a disciple of Grandmaster Feng Zhi Qiang. Nelson has been teaching since 2014. This class is free and open to beginners as well as those who have previous Tai Chi experience. People of all ages are welcome. You must sign in upon arrival.
events.blurb: Learn Tai Chi principles and practice slow, gentle movements with instructor Nelson Ng to build balance and flexibility.

events.title: Pumpkin Pool-ooza
events.description: Celebrate fall with a festive morning at the Blackberry Farm Pools. Pumpkin Pool-ooza features a floating pumpkin patch, swimming, pumpkin decorating, games, music, and seasonal activities for the whole family. Each registered participant can choose a pumpkin from the pool to take home. Costumes are encouraged on the pool deck, but participants must wear a swimsuit to enter the water. Registration and Pricing Cupertino resident $14 Non-resident $18 Registration is required for every person attending Children younger than 12 must be accompanied by a registered parent or guardian.
events.blurb: Swim through a floating pumpkin patch, decorate a pumpkin, and play fall games at Blackberry Farm Pools.

events.title: Tech Mentor / Computer & iPad Assistance
events.description: Tech mentoring and Computer 1-on-1 assistance. A Volunteer Tech Mentor/computer coach will be available to help customers increase their computer skills. Are you a senior trying to catch up with the digital world? Would you like to learn how to create an email, to search the internet, to create and edit Microsoft Word documents, to do online job searching or to complete online job applications? Increase your digital literacy today. Our tech mentors can guide you in learning a variety of computer skills that enable you to better use the library's public computers and to benefit from the library's freely available online resources, including ebooks!. Don't worry about not having a computer, i Pads will be available for in-library use during the mentoring session. Our tech mentor is available on a drop-in schedule. If you have more questions, please call us at 408-808-3053.
events.blurb: Get one-on-one computer and iPad help from a volunteer tech mentor at Pearl Avenue Library.

events.title: Family Storytime + Stay & Play
events.description: Storytime is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities. Storytime is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of reading and learning for all ages. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! After Storytime concludes, we invite you to Stay & Play! Until 6:30 pm the Storytime librarian and special toys will be on the Children's Room floor to keep the fun going. Meet new friends, play with toys, chat, get book recommendations, and maybe even create something! Storytime 5:30-6:00 PM Stay & Play 6:00-6:30 PM Free, with limited capacity. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.attendanceNote: Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of Storytime.
events.blurb: Join stories, songs, rhymes, and movement with the whole family at Seven Trees Library, then stay to play.

events.title: Reading Buddies with Grant
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Children in grades K-5 will discover the joy of reading while improving their reading skills through practice with Grant on Mondays. Our reading buddy will listen to children and help them build confidence in their ability to read. They will ask questions about the books being read to encourage reading comprehension. Children will enjoy one-on-one interaction with Grant who has been trained to create a positive reading experience for beginning and developing readers. Availability of Reading Buddies is on a first-come, first-served basis.
events.attendanceNote: Availability of Reading Buddies is on a first come, first served basis.
events.blurb: Practice reading aloud with volunteer Grant and build confidence one-on-one at King Library.

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club
events.description: Boost your English conversation skills with our volunteer instructor, Ms. Veena, in a welcoming and respectful setting tailored for adult learners. Improve your speaking and listening abilities, broaden your vocabulary, participate in discussions on current events, and more—all at no cost. Pre-registration is required to receive reminder emails and lesson plan details. Due to limited capacity, please arrive on time. If you are more than 5 minutes late, your spot may be given to someone on the waitlist. Thank you for your understanding. Sessions are held weekly in the library's Group Study Room.
events.blurb: Practice conversational English with volunteer instructor Ms. Veena and discuss current events with fellow adult learners.

events.title: Reading Buddies
events.description: Reading Buddies provides students in grades K-3 with an opportunity to improve their reading skills by working one-on-one with a reading coach. Reading Buddies creates a positive reading experience for beginning and developing readers and helps children build confidence as readers. Our reading coach will listen to children read and provide support in reading and comprehension. Students can bring their favorite book or choose from the available selection at the Joyce Ellington Branch Library. Free. Pre-registration not required. However, reading sessions are available on a first-come, first-served basis and the duration of reading sessions may be limited depending on the number of participating students.
events.attendanceNote: Free. Pre-registration not required. However, reading sessions are available on a first come, first served basis and the duration of reading sessions may be limited depending on the number of participating students.
events.blurb: Watch K-3 readers pair with coaches for one-on-one practice at Reading Buddies at Joyce Ellington Library.

events.title: Golden State Valkyries Library Card Launch

Learn more about the partnership at sjpl.org/Valkyries. Request ADA accommodations for this event.
events.blurb: Join activities, giveaways, and a live DJ as the Golden State Valkyries reveal their library card design.

events.title: Reading Partners One-on-One Reading Tutoring
events.description: Free Reading Help for Students in Grades 1–3 Recommended for students in 2nd and 3rd grade. Give your child extra support to become a stronger, more confident reader! Reading Partners provides free one-on-one reading tutoring with trained volunteer tutors. Students meet twice a week for 45-minute sessions and receive personalized, research-based reading support. Program Dates: September 21, 2026 – May 28, 2027 Space is limited, and applications are reviewed to determine if the program is a good fit for your child. Apply Online — It's Free! Ayuda de lectura Gratis para estudiantes de 1. º a 3. º grado Recomendado para estudiantes de 2. º y 3. º grado. ¡Brinde a su hijo/a apoyo adicional para que se convierta en un lector más seguro y exitoso! Reading Partners ofrece tutoría de lectura individual y gratuita con voluntarios capacitados. Los estudiantes se reúnen dos veces por semana en sesiones de 45 minutos y reciben apoyo personalizado de lectura basado en investigaciones. Fechas del programa: 21 de septiembre de 2026 – 28 de mayo de 2027 El espacio es limitado y las solicitudes serán revisadas para determinar si el programa es adecuado para su hijo/a. Solicite en línea — ¡Es Gratis! Hỗ trợ đọc MIỄN PHÍ cho học sinh lớp 1–3 Khuyến khích dành cho học sinh lớp 2 và lớp 3. Hãy giúp con quý vị nhận thêm sự hỗ trợ để trở thành một người đọc tự tin và thành công hơn! Reading Partners cung cấp hỗ trợ đọc một kèm một hoàn toàn miễn phí với các tình nguyện viên đã được đào tạo. Học sinh tham gia hai buổi mỗi tuần, mỗi buổi 45 phút và nhận được sự hỗ trợ đọc cá nhân dựa trên nghiên cứu. Thời gian chương trình: Ngày 21 tháng 9 năm 2026 – ngày 28 tháng 5 năm 2027 Số lượng chỗ có hạn và các đơn đăng ký sẽ được xem xét để xác định chương trình có phù hợp với con quý vị hay không. Đăng ký trực tuyến — Hoàn toàn MIỄN PHÍ!
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited, and applications are reviewed to determine if the program is a good fit for your child.
events.blurb: Get matched with a volunteer tutor for one-on-one reading practice at Evergreen Library.

events.title: Music and Movement in Vietnamese and English and Craft/Múa Hát Song Ngữ Anh
events.description: Bilingual Music and Movement in English and Vietnamese is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities through songs, rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities both in English and Vietnamese. Music and Movement is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of learning for all ages. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! Following the Storytime, kids will learn to make a simple and creative craft to take home! We host Vietnamese Storytime and Craft every Friday, plus a special bilingual session on the fourth Tuesday of each month. Free, no registration is required. Please note that this will be an indoor program. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards. Múa hát song ngữ bằng tiếng Anh và tiếng Việt được thiết kế để phù hợp với nhiều lứa tuổi. Chúng tôi mong muốn mời cả gia đình cùng tham gia vào các hoạt động này để cùng hát các bài đồng dao, cùng vận động ngón tay và cùng nhảy múa vui vẻ. Âm nhạc và nhảy múa là một trải nghiệm thú vị và giúp cho cả gia đình tương tác tốt hơn, thúc đẩy niềm vui học tập cho trẻ em ở mọi lứa tuổi. Mọi người đều được nhiệt liệt chào đón tại chương trình này. Sau phần kể chuyện, các bé sẽ được hướng dẫn làm một món thủ công đơn giản và sáng tạo để mang về nhà! Thứ Sáu hằng tuần có hoạt động kể chuyện và thủ công tiếng Việt; riêng thứ Ba tuần thứ tư hằng tháng sẽ có chương trình kể chuyện song ngữ đặc biệt. Chương trình hoàn toàn miễn phí và không cần phải đăng ký trước.
events.blurb: Sing songs and do movement activities in Vietnamese and English with the whole family at Evergreen Library.

events.title: One-On-One Reading Coach for Kids
events.description: Our One-on-One Reading Tutor for Kids provides students in grades K-3 with an opportunity to improve their reading skills by working one-on-one with a reading coach. Our reading coach creates a positive reading experience for beginning and developing readers and helps children build confidence as readers. Our reading coach will listen to children read and provide support in phonics, sight words, and comprehension. Students can bring their favorite book or choose from the available selection at the Cambrian Branch Library to read aloud to their reading coach. Free. Pre-registration not required. However, reading sessions are available on a first-come, first-served basis and the duration of reading sessions will be 15 minutes. (A little longer session may be permitted, provided there are no other participants). Participants can also use their session to read away their fines! Just inform your coach (open to youth only). Please note, that the One-On-One Reading Tutor for Kids is a program to encourage young readers to practice their reading skills with an adult volunteer. (It is not intended as an hour long tutoring session.)

For 30 minutes following Storytime, special age-appropriate toys will be available for children and caregivers to continue the fun together Storytime: 11:30 a.m. to noon Stay & Play: noon to 12:30 p.m. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards. Tiempo de Cuentos & Stay and Play Tiempo de Cuentos está diseñado para niños pequeños e invita a toda la familia a participar en actividades de alfabetización temprana, como cuentos, rimas, juegos con los dedos y actividades de movimiento. events.title: Make & Decorate Sugar Skulls
events.description: Get ready for Día de los Muertos by making a sugar skull! In this multi-session program, participants will learn to make and then decorate sugar skulls using traditional and modern materials. In the first session, using a special sugar mixture and premade molds, we'll create the parts needed for a sugar skull. In the next session, after the sugar skulls have cured, we'll connect the sugar skull pieces and decorate them with colored frosting, foil, sequins, paint, and more! Once decorated, the sugar skulls will be ready to display on your home altar or our community ofrenda. Please note: creating sugar skulls is a multi-day process. Participants will not be able to finish their skulls in one session and should plan to return for the second session to decorate skulls. Session 1: Tuesday, September 22, 3:30-5:30 PM Session 2: Tuesday, September 29, 3:30-5:30 PM ¡Haz & decora tu propia Calaverita de Azúcar! ¡Ven a celebrar el Día de los Muertos creando una calaverita de azúcar muy especial! En este divertido programa de varias sesiones, aprenderás a hacer y decorar calaveritas usando materiales tradicionales y modernos. En la primera sesión, usaremos una mezcla especial de azúcar y moldes para formar las piezas de la calaverita. En la siguiente sesión, cuando ya estén listas y duritas, uniremos las piezas y las decoraremos con papel de colores, lentejuelas, pintura y mucho más. Al final, podrás llevarte tu calaverita para ponerla en tu altar en casa o en la ofrenda de la comunidad. Importante: Las calaveritas necesitan varios días para estar listas, así que no podrás terminar todo en una sola sesión. ¡Planea regresar a las siguientes para decorarlas! Sesión 1: Miércoles, 22 de septiembre, 3:30-5:30 PM Sesión 2: Miércoles, 29 de septiembre, 3:30-5:30 PM
events.blurb: Mold and decorate a traditional sugar skull ahead of Día de los Muertos at Biblioteca Latinoamericana Library.

events.title: Asistencia tecnologica y ayuda personalizada

events.title: Mahjong Club
events.description: Adults and seniors interested in learning the basics or need a refresher of how to play Taiwanese Mahjong are welcome to join this program. You'll learn while playing the game: - How to set up the game tiles and understand them - The flow of the game - Make sets during the game - How to win it Learning Mahjong improves cognitive function, helps reduce stress and creates a sense of community. Adults and Seniors interested in learning the basics or need a refresher of how to play Chinese Mahjong are welcome to register for this program. You'll learn while playing the game: - How to set up the game tiles and understand them - The flow of the game - Make sets during the game - How to win it Learning Mahjong improves cognitive function, helps reduce stress and creates a sense of community. You will also learn strategy and strengthen communications and sense of community. No registration needed.

events.title: Music and Movement in Vietnamese and English and Craft/Múa Hát Song Ngữ Anh
events.description: Bilingual Music and Movement in English and Vietnamese is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities through songs, rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities both in English and Vietnamese. Music and Movement is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of learning for all ages. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! Following the Storytime, kids will learn to make a simple and creative craft to take home! On the 4th Tuesday of each month, a bilingual story will be read during this program. Free, no registration is required. Please note that this will be an indoor program. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards. Múa hát song ngữ bằng tiếng Anh và tiếng Việt được thiết kế để phù hợp với nhiều lứa tuổi. Chúng tôi mong muốn mời cả gia đình cùng tham gia vào các hoạt động này để cùng hát các bài đồng dao, cùng vận động ngón tay và cùng nhảy múa vui vẻ. Âm nhạc và nhảy múa là một trải nghiệm thú vị và giúp cho cả gia đình tương tác tốt hơn, thúc đẩy niềm vui học tập cho trẻ em ở mọi lứa tuổi. Mọi người đều được nhiệt liệt chào đón tại chương trình này. Sau phần kể chuyện, các bé sẽ được hướng dẫn làm một món thủ công đơn giản và sáng tạo để mang về nhà! Kể chuyện song ngữ và múa hát cùng với làm thủ công vào thứ ba của tuần thứ tư trong tháng. Chương trình hoàn toàn miễn phí và không cần phải đăng ký trước.
events.blurb: Sing, move, and craft with your kids at this bilingual English-Vietnamese music and movement program.

Discover the restorative power of Qigong in this 90-minute group practice, which combines gentle movements, deep rhythmic breathing, and mindful focus to help reduce stress and increase vital energy. The exercises are simple, safe, and suitable for participants of all ages and fitness levels. Shaolin Neijin Yizhichan is a traditional Qigong system originating from the Southern Shaolin Temple in Fujian, China, with over 1,500 years of history. It is an effective practice for quickly enhancing internal energy and promoting spinal health. The method helps open the meridians, regulate qi and blood circulation, and restore balance between yin and yang, supporting overall physical and mental well-being, disease prevention, and longevity. events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents Lessons in Fear
events.description: Does the solution to the conflict between Israelis and Palestinians rest in the classroom rather than in the angry, fearful streets of the region? Can better answers be found in schools rather than political conferences? Lessons in Fear explores Israeli and Palestinian education from the ground up. In a media world obsessed with conflict, Lessons in Fear takes a humanized, behind-the-scenes look at how ordinary kids are educated in one of the world's trouble spots. The film looks carefully at the lives of students and teachers, who find themselves on the front lines intellectually and physically. Their battleground is one of knowledge and self-examination. Their challenges are a deeply engrained culture of violence, the denial of history and legacies of hatred, propaganda and segregation. Lessons in Fear is not a litany of wrongs. The film is a character driven portrait of courage in action as it presents an unvarnished look at the struggle to make education a positive force in Israel and the Palestinian Territories. James Cullingham is an educator, award-winning documentary filmmaker, a widely published writer, and seasoned national broadcaster. Cullingham is coordinator and a professor in the Journalism Broadcast program at the School of Communication Arts of Seneca College in Toronto. His documentaries concerning social justice, politics, history, and popular culture have been screened around the world. Cullingham has been published by Canada's leading newspapers and magazines. He appears as a guest on a number of Canadian public affairs and cultural television programs. In 2003-2005, Cullingham earned a Masters degree in history at the University of Toronto. He is currently pursuing doctoral studies in history at Toronto's York University Ontario with an Honor's Degree in Native Studies and French. He is an accomplished wilderness canoeist and avid hiker. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.

Bring a gently used costume with you to trade for a "new-to-you" option, or simply come and choose from our pre-donated selections! Don't know what a costume swap is? Here are some FAQs and our answers: Q. What is a costume swap? A. Great question! To swap means to trade, so bring a gently used costume to leave behind for another child to enjoy, and pick a "new" one for yourself. Q. If it's a swap, why do you have pre-donated costumes? A. We want to do our best to have choices for you! And also we want every kiddo to join even if they weren't able to bring a costume to trade this time. Q. Will you definitely have my size? A. We cannot guarantee that we will have your size, but hopefully you can find something that works or something to grow into. Q. Will there be scary costumes? A. Possibly. It will be up to you and your library adult to decide what the right costume is for you. Q. What will you do with the costume that I bring if no other child chooses it? A. We will donate it so that it makes its way to a great new owner! If you have other questions, feel free to ask us at the Children's Information Desk. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For October 4th: Topic: Desires - Natural, Necessary, and Unnecessary. Greed for Life and Wealth "Some desires are natural and necessary, others natural but not necessary, still others neither natural nor necessary but generated by senseless whims." Principal Doctrine 29. "A person is made unhappy either by fear or by endless and vain desire. The man who curbs these can attain for himself the blessed gift of reason." Fragment 74. "All desires that do not lead to physical pain if not satisfied are unnecessary, and involve cravings that are easily resolved when they appear to entail harm or when the object of desire is hard to get." Principal Doctrine 30. "Nothing is sufficient for the man to whom the sufficient is too little." Vatican Sayings 68 "Everyone departs this life as though he had only just been born." Vatican Sayings 60. "There is also a limit to frugality. The man unable to consider this suffers a similar end as the man who indulges in excess." Vatican Sayings 63. "Not the youth, but the old man who has lived life well, is to be deemed happy. The youth in his prime is made distraught and baffled by fortune; the old man, as though in port in his old age, has brought safely into harbor the goods he scarcely hoped for before, and has secured them with unfailing gratitude." Vatican Sayings 17. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 5 (pp. 42-53), 10 (pp. 103-115), and 14 (pp. 145-155). Some Questions to Discuss: What is the criterion that Epicurus suggested for discriminating between desires? "What will happen to me if the object of my desire is achieved? What will happen if it is not?" from Epicurus, Vatican Sayings 71. Does Epicurus advise his reader to be ascetic? Can our society accept Epicurus's argument against excessive wealth? Can we offer the alternative argument in support of excessive wealth? In our society, what can drive the desire to live if not forever, then for 300 or even 500 years? (These numbers have been recently stated in interviews with some enthusiasts of longevity research. See, for example, this article ).
events.blurb: Join a friendly discussion questioning ideas about hustle, success, and independence at Rinconada Library.

events.title: Sci-Fi & Fantasy Book Club
events.description: In honor of Hispanic Heritage Month we will be discussing Silver Nitrate by Silvia Moreno-Garcia. You can register and pick up a copy at the adult reference desk. Montserrat has always been overlooked. She's a talented sound editor, but she's left out of the boys' club running the film industry in '90s Mexico City. And she's all but invisible to her best friend, Tristán, a charming if faded soap opera star, though she's been in love with him since childhood. Then Tristán discovers his new neighbor is the cult horror director Abel Urueta, and the legendary auteur claims he can change their lives—even if his tale of a Nazi occultist imbuing magic into highly volatile silver nitrate stock sounds like sheer fantasy. The magic film was never finished, which is why, Urueta swears, his career vanished overnight. He is cursed. Now the director wants Montserrat and Tristán to help him shoot the missing scene and lift the curse... But Montserrat soon notices a dark presence following her, and Tristán begins seeing the ghost of his ex-girlfriend. As they work together to unravel the mystery of the film and the obscure occultist who once roamed their city, Montserrat and Tristán may find that sorcerers and magic are not only the stuff of movies. events.title: San Francisco Opera Guild: Manon preview
events.description: Join us for a preview and presentation by Rebecca Plack of the San Francisco Opera's upcoming performance of Manon by Jules Massenet. Manon is young, beautiful, and has a taste for the finer things … which is why her family is sending her to a convent. En route to her new life, she falls for the handsome Chevalier des Grieux and they run away to Paris, the city of love. But their youthful ardor is threatened by fatherly disapproval, and Manon finds herself with a choice to make: wait alone in poverty or embrace the wealth of a new lover? Manon composer Jules Massenet 's soaring score captures the intensity of young love as Manon and Des Grieux's relationship endures twist after turn. Manon must navigate a path that careens between the radiant glow of love and the allure of wealth. Soprano and musicologist Rebecca Plack is Professor of Opera Studies and Music History at the San Francisco Conservatory of Music; she has also taught at the Vancouver International Song Institute. She has performed solo recitals for the International Great Romantics Festival in Hamilton, Canada, at the ATER Forum Festival in Ferrara, Italy, and at the Franz Liszt Museum in Budapest; she has also given talks and lecture recitals at Oxford University and at meetings of the American Musicological Society. Her opera credits include leading and featured roles with Ithaca Opera and Sacramento Opera, as well as with the Caramoor and Aspen music festivals. She graduated magna cum laude from Princeton University, received her MM from the Manhattan School of Music, and earned her doctorate at Cornell University, where her dissertation explored connections between vocal technique and musical style in recordings of German Lieder. She lives in Davis, CA, where she maintains a private voice studio. Registration means you will receive a reminder email the day before but registration is not required.

(2023) Former FBI Agent Titus Crowne ran for Sheriff in his hometown to change a bigoted local police force. He finds being the first black sheriff in a rural Virginia county no easy task. First when an active shooter at the high school kills a locally beloved high school teacher, and himself as well. Titus' continuing investigations uncover images which reveal that both the killer and his victim were connected through their participation in horrifying sexually ritual killings of seven local black children who matched the descriptions of missing persons police reports over recent years. events.description: Presenter: Amy Yang, certified Qigong instructor, International Neijin Qigong Academy. Instruction will be in English and Mandarin on Thursdays, August 6 through October 8, 2026, from 11 AM to 12:30 PM. Discover the restorative power of Qigong in this 90-minute group practice, which combines gentle movements, deep rhythmic breathing, and mindful focus to help reduce stress and increase vital energy. The exercises are simple, safe, and suitable for participants of all ages and fitness levels. Shaolin Neijin Yizhichan is a traditional Qigong system originating from the Southern Shaolin Temple in Fujian, China, with over 1,500 years of history. It is an effective practice for quickly enhancing internal energy and promoting spinal health. The method helps open the meridians, regulate qi and blood circulation, and restore balance between yin and yang, supporting overall physical and mental well-being, disease prevention, and longevity. events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club: Latine & Hispanic Heritage Month
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph. D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/

events.title: Bring Your Product Ideas to Life Using AI
events.description: Have you ever had an idea to make everyday life easier with a website, an app, or a digital tool, but didn't have the technical skills to build it yourself? Join presenter Viral Parekh as he walks through his own journey building mobile apps with AI, including the challenges he faced and the lessons he learned along the way. Viral is the creator of Banavu Kids Activities Finder App, available on the Apple App Store and Google Play Store, designed to help parents easily find activities for kids. This session includes a hands-on portion where attendees can start bringing their own ideas to life using AI tools in real time. Target Audience Adults (but open to anyone who can use a computer independently) Prerequisites No prior experience required! All you need to bring is: A laptop. If a personal laptop is not available, participants have the option to check out a loaner laptop or Chromebook at the front desk (availability is limited). Free accounts for AI tools such as Chat GPT, Claude, Gemini, or Lovable. We recommend choosing a couple tools (since tokens are limited with free accounts) and downloading the tools before the event. About the Presenter Viral has spent over a decade working on software and hardware technologies at leading Silicon Valley companies, including Apple and Robinhood. During his career, he helped deliver world-class user experiences for products used by hundreds of millions of people every day, including Siri, Air Drop, Apple Pay, and stock trading platforms. A longtime Bay Area resident, Viral now focuses on growing his app and is passionate about giving back to the community by sharing his knowledge and experience.

events.title: Nonfiction Book Discussion: A Higher Call by Adam Makos
events.description: Book Jacket for A Higher Call Open to all adults who love to read and discuss nonfictional literature. In October, the Adult Nonfiction Book Group will discuss the dual biography, A Higher Call: an incredible true story of combat and chivalry in the war-torn skies of WWII. By Adam Makos (2013) Franz Stigler was a commercial pilot drafted into the Luftwaffe at the beginning of World War II, losing many of his friends and contemporaries to death while flying missions over North Africa, Italy and Germany. In December 1943, while on a mission over Germany, Stigler intercepted a badly damaged American B-17, commanded by Charles Brown, the other pilot covered in the biography. Rather than finish off the damaged plane, which would have meant the death of the entire B-17 crew, Stigler instead guided them toward the English Channel and back to safety. 60 years later, Brown and Stigler finally met face to face. The Adult Nonfiction Book Discussion Group meets on the second Sunday of each month at 11 AM in Room 201B For accessibility accommodations (ex. events.title: Writers Helping Writers: From Memoir to Career Planning Book: A Journey of Discovery
events.description: How did a collection of short-story memoirs from the corporate world turn into a full-fledged career-planning book? Join author Korie Pelka for an open, interactive presentation on her wild, nonlinear path to publication. She'll pull back the curtain on how she discovered her voice, pinpointed her target reader, and clarified the impact she wanted her book to make. Expect real talk on all the foibles and missteps along the way—and how you can avoid them in your own journey. Korie Pelka holds a B.F.A. and M.A. in theater directing, which served her well during her 25-year career as a communications professional in Silicon Valley. In 2015 she left the corporate world to discover her own voice in her "third act." Today she is a certified career coach who has helped hundreds of clients navigate meaningful career transitions. Her book, Get Unstuck. Get Clear. Get Going. A Guide to Discovering the Next Stage in Your Career Journey, is a business career-planning book that provides an actionable framework for confidently navigating what's next in your life and career. Korie chronicles her third-act journey and her avid quest for the perfect gelato on her website www.koriepelka.com. California Writers Club-San Francisco Peninsula Branch members share their expertise on writing, editing, marketing, publishing and more. Writers Helping Writers resumes for their fourth year on the third Thursday of these months: October 15 January 21 March 18 May 20 Registration is not required, but if you register, you'll receive an email reminder the day before the event.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For October 18th: Topic: Desires - Natural, Necessary, and Unnecessary. Success, Ambition, Sex "One who understands the limits of the good life knows that what eliminates the pains brought on by need and what makes the whole of life perfect is easily obtained, so that there is no need for enterprises that entail the struggle for success." Principal Doctrine 21. "Great abundance is heaped up as the result of brutalizing labor, but a miserable life is the result." Fragment 73. "If there is intense striving after those physical desires that do not lead to pain if unfulfilled, this is because they arise from idle opinion; they fail to be dispelled, not because of their own nature but because of the vain fancies of humankind." Principal Doctrine 30. "Happiness and blessedness do not belong to abundance of riches or exalted position or offices or power, but to freedom from pain and gentleness of feeling and a state of mind that sets limits that are in accordance with nature." Fragment 85. "I learn from your letter that carnal disturbances make you excessively inclined to sexual intercourse. Well, so long as you do not break any laws or disturb well-established conventions or annoy any of your neighbors or wear down your body or use up your funds, you may carry out your own plans as you like. However, it is impossible not to be affected by at least one of these things. Sex never benefited any man, and it's a marvel if it hasn't injured him!" Vatican Sayings 51. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 13 (pp. 137-144) and 16 (pp. 171-179). Some Questions to Discuss: What effect do competitive relations and ambitions have on us as individuals and as a society? What does it mean to be successful for Epicurus? What would be counted as success in our society? How do we reason our understanding of success? Would we agree with Epicurus's argument on sexual desire?
events.blurb: Join a friendly discussion questioning ideas about hustle, success, and independence at Rinconada Library.

events.title: Neurosphere: Neuroscience and More! Grades 3-8
events.description: Come join teen-led group Neuro Sphere! Neuro Sphere is a community for curious 2nd-7th graders about medicine! This session will dive into the basics of brain function, fun activities to test your brainpower, and an introduction to future career opportunities. There will be snacks- feel free to bring a friend! We're a group of high school students driven by a passion for neuroscience and the wonders of the brain. events.title: Author Event: Book launch for Bruce Overby's latest novel
events.description: Join us for an evening with local writer Bruce Overby ( The Cyclone Release and recently released Tristan 4 America ) with Geri Spieler ( Housewife Assassin, Regina of Warsaw ) serving as moderator. Bruce Overby is a fiction writer with particular interest in issues of loss and belonging, family and relationships, the human condition in a technology-driven world, and addiction. His fiction has appeared in Storyglossia, the Green Mountains Review, the Evening Street Review, and the anthology Home of the Brave: Stories in Uniform from Press53. " Bookmarks," the story of a brother's struggle with alcoholism, his love of poetry, and the sometimes disturbing mix of the two, won first prize in the Lorian Hemingway Short Story Competition. Bruce's debut novel, The Cyclone Release, was a finalist in the Blue Moon Novel Competition and is available now from Madville Publishing. His second novel, Tristan 4 America, is forthcoming from Willow River Press in October 2026. Bruce is a graduate of the MFA in Writing Program at Queens University of Charlotte. A San Jose native, Bruce is a member of California Writers Club-SF Peninsula Branch and participated in Rinconada Library's inaugural book fair in April. Books will be available for purchase. Bring your questions!

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 1st: Topic: Epicurus's Advice: Make Friends and Be Frank with Them "Every friendship is desirable for itself, but it has its origin in personal advantage." Vatican Sayings 23. "We do not need the help of our friends so much as the confidence that our friends will help us." Vatican Sayings 34. "The man continually seeking help is no friend, nor is the one who never links help with friendship. For the one barters kindness for favors, while the other cuts off hope for the future." Vatican Sayings 39. "Of all the things that wisdom provides for the happiness of the whole man, by far the most important is the acquisition of friendship." Principal Doctrine 27. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 6 (pp. 54-65) and 7 (pp. 66-79). Some Questions to Discuss: What are the two main qualities that make a relationship a friendship, according to Emily Austin's analysis of Epicurus's views on friendship? [Austin, 56-7] Austin says that "a shared sense of what truly matters" [64] is a core condition for friendship. What is the meaning of this condition? Do our current ideas about friendship coincide with those of Epicurus? What do we value in friendship? What is "frank speech" for you? Why can we be uncomfortable with telling a friend the truth? What is the reason for feeling this way? Can we be frank even with ourselves? A friend vs. Psychologist: where does your preference lie and why?
events.blurb: Join a friendly discussion questioning ideas about hustle, success, and independence at Rinconada Library.

events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Spies Among Us
events.description: This is a rare look into the inner workings of a data-driven surveillance state run by one of the most feared secret police forces the world has ever known – East Germany's Stasi. A personal investigation into family secrets by Peter Keup, a Stasi victim-turned-historian, takes a turn when he contacts the men who ran the system. These are the first dialogues between Stasi officers and a victim ever recorded. Through these encounters a terrifying mosaic is built of the lengths people go to maintain power in a dictatorship, as well as the indomitable human spirit that seeks truth and self-determination. Jamie Coughlin Silverman and Gabriel Silverman are award-winning journalists-turned-documentary filmmakers. Their first feature documentary, Transmilitary, won the Audience Award for Best Documentary at Sxsw and received critical acclaim. Trans Military was represented by Cinetic Media and distributed by Gravitas Ventures. It premiered on Logo TV and Amazon Prime. The film screened at more than 100 film festivals worldwide, and the Silvermans were named to the 2018 Top 10 Filmmakers to Watch list by The Independent. The Silvermans are Gotham (IFP) Documentary Lab Fellows, CNN/Film Independent Episodic Lab Fellows. Their work has been supported by the International Documentary Association, Catapult Film Fund, Jonathan Logan Family Foundation, and Frameline Completion Fund. They are the first recipients of funding from the GLAAD Media Institute. Their production company, Side XSide Studios, is a global documentary firm that specializes in consequential and high-visibility non-fiction storytelling. Prior to Side XSide Studios, the Silvermans worked in leading newsrooms. Gabe was a video journalist at The Washington Post where his work was recognized with more than a dozen awards, including an Edward R. Murrow Award for his investigative work, a White House News Photographers Award for Best Documentary, and two Emmy nominations. Jamie was the supervising producer for USA Today Sports, where she led editorial and branded video content strategy. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.blurb: Watch a documentary tracing Stasi surveillance in East Germany through Peter Keup's personal investigation into family secrets.
