events.title: Pageturners: What We Can Know by Ian McEwan
events.description: Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting International Booker Prize winner Andrey Kurkov ( Diary of an Invasion ) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. Our reading list for 2026 follows: My Friends by Fredrik Bachman - January The Wager: A Tale of a Shipwreck, Mutiny and Murder by David Grann - February South of the Border, West of the Sun by Haruki Murakami - March Trespassers at the Golden Gate: A True Account of Love, Murder, and Madness in Gilded-Age San Francisco by Gary Krist - April The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui - May The Wedding People by Alison Espach - June Unlikely Animals: A Novel by Annie Hartnett - July Say Nothing: A True Story of Murder and Memory in Northern Ireland by Patrick Radden Keefe - August The Frozen River by Ariel Lawhon - September We'll Prescribe You a Cat by Syou Ishida - October What We Can Know by Ian McEwan - November The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon - December. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph. D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 15th: Topic: An Epicurean in Public Life: Justice and Injustice "Justice's greatest reward is peace of mind." Fragment 80. "Justice was never an entity in itself. It is a kind of agreement not to harm or be harmed, made when men associate with each other at any time and in communities of any size whatsoever." Principal Doctrine 33. "Injustice is not an evil in itself. It's evil lies in the anxious fear that you will not elude those who have authority to punish such misdeeds." Principal Doctrine 34. "It is impossible to leave the pleasant life without also living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely it is impossible to live sensibly, nobly, and justly without living pleasantly. A person who does not have a pleasant life is not living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely the person who does not have these virtues cannot live pleasantly." Principal Doctrine 5. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 8 (pp. 80-91). Some Questions to Discuss: Based on the ideas expressed in the Principal Doctrines, what is Epicurus's view on the source of justice in society? What is the connection that Epicurus draws between injustice and corrosive desires according to Austin's analysis of his views on injustice? Is it easy to be just? Is it hard to be unjust?
events.blurb: Join a friendly reading and discussion group at the library tackling big questions about how we live and what we value.

events.title: Master Gardeners: Planning and Planting a Little Fruit Orchard
events.description: Please join us for an informative workshop presented by UC Master Gardeners of Santa Clara County. So you want to plant fruit trees, excellent! What kind? Are you looking for plums, apricots, peaches, apples or something less common? There are hundreds of varieties of each, how do you choose? How big should the tree be? (There is actually a correct answer!) What are chill hours and how many are good? Semi-dwarf? True dwarf? Multi-graft? How do I plant a new tree? Local nurseries will begin stocking bare root fruit trees in December. Come learn what decisions affect the success of your orchard. Don Bollinger leads the orchard team at the Master Gardener demonstration garden at Martial Cottle Park in South San Jose. He leads year-round hands-on learning and demonstrations of fruit tree management including winter pruning, water, fertilizer, pest management, soil health and fruit variety selection. No need to register, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.
events.blurb: Learn from UC Master Gardeners how to choose, plan, and plant fruit trees for a home orchard.

There will be snacks- feel free to bring a friend! We're a group of high school students driven by a passion for neuroscience and the wonders of the brain. Our mission is to inspire curiosity and spark a love for science in younger students by creating engaging, hands-on learning experiences. Through Neuro Sphere, we hope to share our knowledge, connect with the community, and encourage the next generation of future scientists and innovators! Questions? Email neurosphereyouth@gmail.com This program is open for 2nd-7th graders only.
events.blurb: Explore brain function and test your brainpower with hands-on activities at this teen-led Neuro Sphere session.

events.title: Author Event with Dr. Carol Peyser
events.description: Please join us to hear Dr, Carol Peyser discuss her book, A Hidden Fate (She Writes Press, October 27, 2026), a literary novel interweaving multiple themes: the emotional consequences of genetic foreknowledge, the weight of family secrets and deceptions, overcoming childhood trauma, and the unexpected conflicts of vision and conviction that can emerge in love relationships. The novel has received a starred Kirkus review, and a Book Life reviewer described it as "great for fans of Lisa Genova's Inside the O'Briens and Abraham Verghese's The Covenant of Water." Early in her career, she directed the Huntington's Disease Clinic at Johns Hopkins Hospital right when predictive testing became available to people at risk for the terrible disease. Dr. Peyser saw first-hand how genetic knowledge — and even the possibility of obtaining it — alters a person's relationship to their future and to their family. Interacting with people deciding what they wanted, or might not want, to know about their future seared these issues into my heart. Later, as a geriatric psychiatrist on the Stanford faculty and in private practice in Menlo Park, she saw these questions multiply. Descendants of those with Alzheimer's disease, major depression, and other heritable illnesses grappled with fears about genetic risk — and with the weight of what to keep private, and what to disclose — to whom, and when. These questions of genetic knowledge, secrecy, and their consequences are at the heart of the book. H ow does wondering what might be coded in our DNA impact us? How does knowing what lies in our genes change us? How are families impacted by the new possibilities genomic testing raises?
events.blurb: Hear Dr. Carol Peyser discuss her novel A Hidden Fate about family secrets and genetic foreknowledge.

events.title: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1: Drawing with Time and Rhythm
events.description: In this one-hour figure-drawing workshop, participants will draw together with pencils for 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 minute—and sometimes even 30 seconds. We will begin with longer drawing times and slowly move to shorter, faster ones. Participants can try different pencil pressure, movement, and speed as the timing changes. Participants may volunteer to pose for the group. As we draw, we will watch different poses and body movements and follow the changing rhythm together. The timing will be repeated about three times. Participants will make several drawings on 11 × 14-inch paper and one larger drawing on 18 × 24-inch paper, arranging several figures on one sheet. The workshop is open to adults of all levels. No drawing experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi Materials: All materials will be provided, including 4B pencils, five sheets of 11 × 14-inch paper, and one sheet of 18 × 24-inch paper for each participant. Durateion: 60 minutes

events.title: Wee Love Art: Fall Leaf Sensory Painting in Baggies
events.description: Explore the colors and textures of autumn leaves in our sensory painting program! Using leaf-shaped cardstock and fall-inspired colors, children will create unique artworks while enhancing fine motor skills and fostering creativity. Guided by our librarians, kids will experiment with paint mixing and texture blending, promoting cognitive and social development. Join us for a fun-filled morning celebrating fall creativity!
events.blurb: Create sensory paintings using leaf-shaped cardstock and fall colors in this hands-on program for kids.

events.title: Self-Help for the Elderly Information Table
events.description: Learn about assistance the nonprofit organization Self-Help for the Elderly offers seniors, including in the following areas. Caregiving Senior Housing Activity Centers Employment Services Social Services Cleaning Services Nutrition Services Health Insurance Counseling and Advocacy Program (HICAP) Digital Learning Program The information table is in the library lobby. Free. No Registration Required. selfhelpelderly.
events.blurb: Learn about caregiving, housing, employment, and health insurance counseling services for seniors at this information table.

events.title: Saturday Board Games Day
events.description: Drop in for a full day of modern board gaming at the Downtown Library! The group meets every 1st Saturday from 10 AM–6 PM. Attendees can bring their own games to play or jump-in with others. Please bring your own snacks and drinks to fuel an afternoon of marathon gaming in the El Camino Room. Presented by The Bay Area Boardgames Meetup Group. Masks are not required in the Palo Alto Libraries, but are recommended.
events.blurb: Bring your own board games or jump into a group game during a marathon gaming session at the library.

events.title: Crochet Club
events.description: Whether you're picking up a hook for the first time or you're a seasoned pro, come stitch with us! Work on your own project, start something new, or learn the basics with help from our knowledgeable volunteer. It's a relaxed, creative space to build skills and connect with fellow crochet lovers of all ages. Hooks, yarn, and basic supplies provided while supplies last. Ages 8 and up. All skill levels welcome.
events.blurb: Bring your own crochet project or learn the basics from a volunteer in a relaxed stitching circle.

events.title: Line Dancing for Beginners/Improvers
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Join our wonderful volunteer instructor Audrey Chen for line dancing classes. Have fun and enjoy music while performing calorie-burning dance movements! Some line dancing experience is preferred but not required. Please note this will be an indoor program. Tuesdays,, 1:30 PM - 3:00 PM August: 11, 18, 25 September: 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 Free! First-time participants at this library will need to sign a waiver form.
events.blurb: Learn line dance steps with volunteer instructor Audrey Chen at West Valley Library on Tuesday afternoons.

events.title: Make Your Own Movie Trailer!
events.description: Come and make your own movie trailer! Discover the different genres of movie trailer templates i Movie has to offer. Participants will learn how to make their own Hollywood-style trailers. We will be using i Pads and i Movie software. Learn how to plan, edit, and share a short creative video project from start to finish. Recommended for ages 7+. Free. Limited materials available. First-come, first-served.
events.attendanceNote: Free. Limited materials available. First come, first served.
events.blurb: Use iPads and iMovie to plan, edit, and share your own Hollywood-style movie trailer.

events.title: Children's Area Scavenger Hunts
events.description: Pick up a checklist at the table in the Children's Area. Look for the images around the Children's Area. Once you have found all of the images on the checklist, come to the table in the Children's Area for a prize (while supplies last!) Themes vary each week. Free. No registration required. While supplies last. This will take place in the Children's Area from 1 PM-2 PM. No scavenger hunt on 11/07/2026.
events.blurb: Grab a checklist and hunt for hidden images around the Children's Area to win a small prize.

events.title: Jack O'Lantern Jamboree!
events.description: We're throwing a Halloween dance party and YOU'RE invited! Children and their families are invited to come decked out in costume and dance with us in the Secret Garden of Children's Library*. We will also have fun crafts and light refreshments. Bring the whole family and join us for this special event! Registration is not required. *In the event of rain, this event will take place in the Treetop Room.
events.blurb: Dance in costume with your family at a Halloween party in the Secret Garden of Children's Library.

events.title: Clases de inglés para Hispanos - Nivel 1
events.description: ¿Quieres mejorar tu vocabulario en Inglés, aprender gramática y hacer amigos? Te invitamos a participar en esta clase de Inglés nivel cero dirigida por la voluntaria Christin. Esta clase es solamente para personas cuyo primer idioma es el Español. ¡Inscríbete ahora, espacio es limitado! Gratis. Se proporcionará el material educativo. Para mayor información escribe a marcela.guevara@sjlibrary.org
events.blurb: Build English vocabulary, learn grammar, and meet other Spanish-speaking learners in this beginner-level class.

events.title: Gentle Yoga / Yoga Relajante
events.description: Discover a soothing practice designed for all bodies and all levels. Gentle Yoga invites you to relax, restore, and feel better from the inside out. Free. No registration required. Bring your own mat. Explora una práctica relajante creada para todos los cuerpos y niveles. El Yoga relajante te invita a restaurarte y reconectar contigo mismo. Gratis. No necesita registrarse. Trae tu propio tapete.
events.blurb: Move through a gentle yoga practice designed for all bodies and levels, offered in English and Spanish.

events.title: Baby Wearing Dance
events.description: Bring your baby and a baby carrier and learn a dance to popular tunes. Expectant mothers are welcome too! For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
events.blurb: Bring your baby in a carrier and learn a dance routine set to popular tunes.

events.title: Lego Club!
events.description: Come join us every Sunday for Lego Club! We have tons of Lego bricks for you to build and explore! Duplo bricks are also available for our younger friends. Want to push yourself and try something a little more difficult? Ask the librarian for a Lego Challenge! Important: Children under 5 must be accompanied by their parents as small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards.
events.blurb: Build with a huge collection of Lego and Duplo bricks and try a librarian-issued Lego Challenge.

events.title: Family Craft: Bean and Lentil Mosaics
events.description: Choose from a variety of beans and lentils to create your own colorful mosaic! Children ages 4–11 are invited to make a unique design using paper, glue, beans, and lentils. All materials will be provided. Family Craft events are designed for children and their adult companions to enjoy together. Crafts will be available while supplies last, so please arrive on time.
events.blurb: Design a colorful mosaic from beans and lentils in this hands-on family craft session.

events.title: Master Gardeners: Native Plants for Pollinators
events.description: Check out how to work in harmony with nature by selecting California native plants that support local ecosystems, conserve resources, and provide food and shelter for pollinators, birds, and other wildlife. Master gardener Mint Pasakdee will share her experience on "Habitat Gardening" or "Backyard Restoring." Gardeners of all levels are welcome. Bring questions.
events.blurb: Hear Master Gardener Mint Pasakdee share tips for planting natives that support local pollinators and wildlife.

events.title: Knitting/Crocheting/Tatting/Bobbin Lace Club
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Do you enjoy working with knitting, crocheting, or tatting? Do you want to learn how, see what others are working on, refine your skills, or talk about all kinds of hand needle crafts? Join us in the East San Jose Carnegie Branch Community Room every week. Everyone 7 and up is invited to participate, and younger children are welcome to accompany their families.
events.blurb: Bring your knitting, crocheting, tatting, or bobbin lace project and swap tips with fellow crafters in the community room.

events.description: Join Librarian Heidi on Friday mornings at 10:30 AM for Family Storytime at Downtown Library. Come sing, rhyme, and read stories with us! While this storytime will be geared towards those older than 2 years, all ages are welcome! Make sure to follow us on YouTube for more stories, songs and rhymes, including a playlist of all of our favorite songs to sing!
events.blurb: Sing, rhyme, and hear stories with Librarian Heidi at Family Storytime on Friday mornings.

events.description: Are you an expert at video, board, and card games? Do you want to demonstrate your skills, or just want to learn the basics? Or maybe you'd like to sink the 8 ball at a game of pool? Join us in the Teen Room at the Hillview Branch Library if you want to play video, board, and card games, play some pool, or just hang out! Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Play video, board, and card games in the Teen Room, or challenge friends to a game of pool.

events.title: STEM Wednesday: Building Bridges
events.description: Join us for the interactive program about bridges and their importance as routes connecting places, people, and communities. Children will learn about bridge types, famous bridges around the world, and why bridges stay strong and safe. They will get a chance to think like civil engineers with hands-on projects and a quiz! Free. Registration required.
events.blurb: Learn about bridge types and engineering while building your own model bridge like a civil engineer.

Mayor Kitty Moore is hosting a Monthly Chat Series in Cupertino throughout 2026, inviting residents and local businesses to discuss any topic with one of the City's decision-makers. These informal gatherings offer a welcoming space for meaningful conversation and community connection.

Presented by Dhyan Foundation, dedicated to promoting physical, mental and spiritual well-being through authentic yogic practices and community education.
events.blurb: Try guided meditation and simple standing or chair-based stretches led by the Dhyan Foundation.

events.title: Cupertino Fall Bike Fest
events.description: Strap on a helmet and bike to Civic Center Plaza to start the fall with some bike-themed fun! The event will feature bike rides, on-bike and off-bike games, arts and crafts, food and beverages for sale, and much more! Check out the Bike Fest website for the schedule, list of events, and registration form: www.cupertino.gov/bikefest
events.blurb: Bike to Civic Center Plaza for group rides, on-bike games, crafts, and food trucks at the Fall Bike Fest.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy a small group interaction with our volunteer and it will be held under the Read to Children sign, within the Children's Area. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Watch kids read to a volunteer in a small group under the Read to Children sign at Berryessa Library.

events.description: Join us every Sunday at 1:00 p.m. at the Joyce Ellington Branch for a fun afternoon of board games! Choose from our large selection of games, including exciting new favorites and classic games that are fun for all ages. Bring your family and friends, roll the dice, and enjoy some friendly competition! No Registration Required.
events.blurb: Choose from a large selection of board games and play with family and friends at the library.

events.title: Tuesday Crochet Get Together
events.description: Tuesday Crochet Get-Together with the Mt Pleasant Neighborhood Library, an event where participants get together to start or finish their own crochet project as well as meet other crocheters. Casual crochet meet-up. Participants are welcome to bring their own materials. This is an adult crochet program for ages 18 and older.
events.blurb: Bring your yarn and hook to work on a crochet project alongside neighbors at Mt. Pleasant Library.

events.title: Indian Classical Dance Program
events.description: Saratoga Library presents dance performances by accomplished Bay area classical dancers. The Bharatanatyam dances presented by Abhirami Shankar 1:15 PM - 2:45 PM Meenakshi Ganesan 3 PM - 4:30 PM The event will take place in the Saratoga Community Room. Thanks to Friends of the Saratoga Libraries for sponsoring this program.
events.blurb: Watch Bharatanatyam performances by Bay Area classical dancers Abhirami Shankar and Meenakshi Ganesan in the Community Room.

events.title: Nameless Anime Club
events.description: Do you enjoy anime and manga? Join Edenvale Branch Library's Nameless Anime Club every fourth Sunday of the month! Enjoy classic anime from the past, new series from today, and make new friends! Participants are welcome to drop in anytime during our program. We hope to see you there! Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Drop in to watch classic and current anime episodes and meet other fans at Edenvale Library.

events.title: Financial Health and Wellness: Fulfilling Long Term Goals
events.description: Join the Library as we welcome financial wellness instructor Brad Hamada of the Heartland Institute of Financial Education back for a series workshop on financial health and wellness! Registration opens two weeks before the event date and is preferred for each individual session to adequately accommodate seating.
events.blurb: Hear financial wellness instructor Brad Hamada walk through strategies for reaching your long term financial goals.

events.title: Excel Basics
events.description: New to Microsoft Excel? This beginner-friendly workshop will introduce you to the essentials, including navigating spreadsheets, entering and formatting data, creating simple formulas, and organizing information. Get comfortable with Excel and build the skills you need to confidently tackle everyday tasks. Free.
events.blurb: Learn to navigate spreadsheets, enter data, and build simple formulas in this beginner Excel workshop.

events.title: Board Game Zone
events.description: Join us every Sunday between 2:00 - 4:00 PM at the Seven Trees Library to play fun board games! We have a large selection to choose from, including new games and classic games that everyone of all ages can enjoy. No Registration Required. Thanks to the Friends of the Seven Trees Library for making this possible!
events.blurb: Pick from a large selection of new and classic board games to play with all ages welcome.

events.title: Celebrate Native American Heritage Month! Story and Craft
events.description: Join Librarian Jennifer as we celebrate Native American Heritage Month! We'll be sharing Native American folk tales, then crafting traditional clay pinch pots. Please note that while all ages are welcome, this program is designed for children ages 5 and up. Space and supplies are limited; please arrive on time!
events.blurb: Hear Native American folk tales and craft a clay pinch pot at Palo Alto's Children's Library.

events.title: Crochet Club
events.description: All are welcome—from beginners to experienced enthusiasts. Bring your own project or start a new one as we refine our skills and discuss all things crochet. A volunteer is available to provide instructions, and offer advice to beginners. Tools and supplies are provided. The minimum age is six years old.
events.blurb: Bring your own crochet project or start something new with guidance from a volunteer instructor.

events.title: ESL Conversation Club for English Language Learners (ELL)
events.description: Practice and improve your English-speaking skills in a group setting with a volunteer facilitator, discussing a variety of topics. A basic understanding of English is required. The purpose of this group is to help learners practice speaking and build confidence and comfort when communicating in English.
events.blurb: Build confidence speaking English with a volunteer facilitator at Joyce Ellington Library's conversation club.

events.title: Basic English Level 1
events.description: Learn the basics of English in an inclusive and welcoming environment! You will: • Learn basic vocabulary • Understand simple grammar • Read simple texts and write basic sentences Lớp này sẽ được giảng dạy bởi một giáo viên có khả năng song ngữ Anh-Việt. Free. Registration requested, but not required.
events.blurb: Build basic English vocabulary and grammar and practice reading and writing simple sentences with a bilingual teacher.

events.title: LEGO Club
events.description: Visit the library every Tuesday for an hour of fun building with LEGO Bricks! Explore your creativity and utilize your engineering skills to build towers, spaceships, forts, and more! This event is recommended for children 5 and older. Small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards for younger children.
events.blurb: Build towers, spaceships, and forts out of LEGO Bricks during an hour of open building time.

events.title: Pizza and Politics
events.address: Cupertino Community Hall, 10350 Torre Ave, Cupertino, CA, 95014
events.description: Pizza and Politics is an award-winning, youth-led biannual pre-election political forum coordinated by youth for youth. The event encourages youth and teen civic engagement, makes politics more accessible, and provides young people with the opportunity to connect directly with politicians.
events.blurb: Watch teens question local politicians and dig into election issues over pizza at Community Hall.

events.title: Board Game Sunday!
events.description: Everyone is invited to play board games! Join us on the second Sunday of the month from 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM. We have board games for all ages: adults, teens, and children. Come with friends & family! (The room closes at 3:30 PM, so come early enough to have time to finish your game.)
events.blurb: Sit down with friends and family to play board games for all ages at the library.

events.title: Chinese Orchestra
events.description: This is an Open Rehearsal featuring the Chinese Erhu (the Erhu is a traditional two-stringed bowed musical instrument often referred to as the "Chinese violin"). The public is invited to observe the preparation process for an upcoming performance and participate in a Q&A session.
events.blurb: Watch an open rehearsal of the Chinese Orchestra featuring erhu players and ask questions during the Q&A.

events.blurb: Sing along and hear stories with Librarian Juliana at this family storytime at Mitchell Park Library.

events.title: Wii Gaming for Tweens and Teens
events.description: Join us for Nintendo Wii fun! We have games available such as Mario Kart, Pac-Man Party, and New Carnival Games. This program is for tweens and teens, ages 8-17. Held in Study Room 2. Registration required. Please note our equipment can only accommodate 4 players at a time.
events.blurb: Play Mario Kart, Pac-Man Party, and other Wii games with fellow tweens and teens in Study Room 2.

events.title: ESL Writing Club
events.description: Practice basic writing skills in English with our tutor in a welcoming and respectful environment for adult learners. Sessions will include creating simple sentence structures, some basic grammar, and build up to writing a simple paragraph. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Practice basic English writing skills with a tutor, from simple sentences to full paragraphs.

events.title: Vietnamese Class for Kids
events.description: Are you between the ages of 5-12 and want to learn Vietnamese? Tully Branch Library will be offering a class for children to learn basic Vietnamese language, grammar, spelling, dictation, writing, and reading. In person registration required at Tully Library.
events.blurb: Learn basic Vietnamese vocabulary, grammar, and writing in a class designed for kids ages 5-12.

events.description: Come learn to play chess, or just play a game! This is an informal and welcoming program for kids up to age 12 and their families. Chess Club meets every Monday. Please check the website event listing for possible date cancellations and library holidays.
events.blurb: Learn chess moves or jump into a casual game with other kids and families.

events.title: Halloween Karaoke Night
events.description: Join us for a night of hauntingly good tunes, thrilling performances, and ghoulish fun! Dress up, sing loud, and let the spirits of music take over. Open to all ages! Registration is not required, but if you do register, you'll receive an email reminder.
events.blurb: Sing your favorite tunes in costume at a Halloween-themed karaoke night open to all ages.

events.title: LEGO Club
events.description: Come join us at Cambrian Branch Library for our LEGO Club! We'll supply both big and small pieces, so come and bring your creativity. Children under 5 must be accompanied by their parents as small pieces can be choking hazards. No registration required.
events.blurb: Build with big and small LEGO pieces supplied at the library, with parents on hand for little ones.

events.description: Children, teens, and their families are invited to play a selection of board games and card games. The games included will be a mix of strategy-based games, educational games, and luck-based games. Come together to have fun with friends and family!

events.title: Online Author Talk: Veronica Roth
events.description: A single choice can transform your destiny. Join us for an online conversation with #1 New York Times bestselling author Veronica Roth as we celebrate the enduring legacy of her Divergent series, one of the most iconic young adult series of a generation, and get an exclusive sneak peek into her highly anticipated upcoming novel, The Sixth Faction! Fifteen years after readers first stepped into dystopian Chicago alongside Tris Prior, the Divergent universe continues to captivate readers with its unflinching exploration of identity, courage, and sacrifice. And in the alternate universe of The Sixth Faction, we revisit familiar characters in a completely new way… Beatrice Prior stands on the brink of a decision every person in her world must make: five factions, five futures, five lives. She has a plan: she's going to make the bravest choice and leave Abnegation to join Dauntless, even though it means abandoning her family. But when tragedy strikes at her choosing ceremony, everything changes—her world, her plans, even Beatrice herself. Her decision will thrust her into the crosshairs of an underground rebellion, where a boy with secrets as dangerous as her own—a boy with only a number for a name—may be the only person she can trust. One choice will change everything. About the Author: Veronica Roth is the #1 New York Times best-selling author of numerous titles including When Among Crows, Chosen Ones, the Divergent series, Carve the Mark and the upcoming Seek the Traitor's Son. Veronica lives with her husband and their dog in Chicago, a city that she lovingly features (and frequently destroys) in many of her novels.
events.blurb: Hear Veronica Roth talk about the Divergent series and get a preview of what's coming next.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Carolyn Russo
events.description: Join us for a captivating online conversation with acclaimed author and Smithsonian curator Carolyn Russo as we dive into her fascinating book, The Ascent of Rauschenberg. Explore the towering legacy, unexpected inspirations, and creative heights of one of America's most influential artistic icons. Most famous for his groundbreaking "Combines"—painting and sculpture hybrids that often incorporated everyday objects—American artist Robert Rauschenberg (1925-2008) created within a range of mediums, including collage, performance, photography, and printmaking. But a connective tissue through it all was his fascination with flight. The Ascent of Rauschenberg explores the flight motif across his work, spanning birds, insects, aviation, spaceflight, sensory experiences, and metaphors for his own life. More than 150 images reveal the vibrant scope of his work, from lithographs inspired by the Apollo 11 launch that NASA invited him to witness and document, to a Combine featuring a taxidermied eagle that evokes Roman mythology. Nine accompanying essays reflect on his many flight themes and subtleties that might otherwise be overlooked. The book also includes archival photographs and personal papers from the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation. About the Author: Carolyn Russo is curator of the art collection at the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum. She has lectured internationally on the subject of art and flight and is the author of several publications including The Ascent of Rauschenberg: Reinventing the Art of Flight, Art of the Airport Tower, In Plane View: Abstractions of Flight, and Women and Flight: Portraits of Contemporary Women Pilots.
events.blurb: Hear Smithsonian curator Carolyn Russo discuss her book on Rauschenberg's creative legacy.

events.title: Concert: Music at Kohl Mansion presents Escher String Quartet
events.description: Now in our fourth year of partnership with Music at Kohl Mansion, we proudly present the Escher String Quartet. The Escher String Quartet has established itself as one of the most accomplished chamber ensembles of its generation. Formed in New York City in 2005, and named after the Dutch graphic artist M.C. Escher, the quartet is celebrated for performances that combine technical brilliance, interpretive insight, and a distinctive ensemble sound. The group serves as Artists of the Chamber Music Society of Lincoln Center and has earned international recognition for its commitment to both the core string quartet repertoire and contemporary music. The quartet has appeared at many of the world's leading concert halls and festivals, including London's Wigmore Hall, Amsterdam's Concertgebouw, the Kennedy Center, Paris's Auditorium du Louvre, and major chamber music festivals throughout North America, Europe, Australia, and Asia. Praised by critics for their precision, warmth, and expressive depth, the Escher String Quartet has received numerous honors, including the prestigious Avery Fisher Career Grant and Lincoln Center's Martin E. Segal Award. The ensemble's critically acclaimed recording projects include the complete string quartets of Alexander Zemlinsky and Felix Mendelssohn and more. Through its adventurous programming and consistently compelling performances, the Escher String Quartet continues to be recognized as one of the leading chamber ensembles on the international stage.
events.blurb: Hear the Escher String Quartet perform chamber music at Music at Kohl Mansion.

events.title: Am I Being Tracked?: A Guide to Digital Privacy
events.description: Registration is required. Every click, search, and scroll leaves a trail but how much of your life is actually being monitored, and by whom? In "Am I Being Tracked?", we take a hype-free look at the modern tracking ecosystem. First, we'll debunk some myths around online privacy. Next, we'll reframe how you think about digital privacy, shifting the goal from "total invisibility" to smart data management. Finally, you'll get a practical checklist of steps you can take right now to gain control over your personal data. About the Presenter: Iman Saleh is a local Mountain View mom and a privacy professional with more than 24 years of experience in big tech and academia. She holds a Ph D in Software Engineering and is recognized as a Fellow of Information Privacy by the International Association of Privacy Professionals (IAPP).
events.blurb: Learn how online tracking actually works and hear the myths around digital privacy debunked in this online session.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Cherie Dimaline
events.description: Step into the atmospheric and deeply moving world of storytelling with acclaimed Métis author Cherie Dimaline as we discuss her captivating body of work and her haunting Young Adult novel, Funeral Songs for Dying Girls. Set in a cemetery shed where sixteen-year-old Winifred lives with her dad, Funeral Songs for Dying Girls follows a teen whose attempt to save her father's job leads to a fake ghost rumor—and accidentally summons a very real, opinionated spirit named Phil. Through this eerie yet heartwarming story, Dimaline crafts a haunting masterpiece about grief, survival, identity, and unexpected connections across the boundary of life and death. Beyond her graveyard-set YA novel, we will explore Dimaline's expansive literary career—from the groundbreaking dystopian survival narrative of The Marrow Thieves and its sequel Hunting by Stars, to the dark, magic-infused folklore of her adult novels like Empire of Wild and Ven Co. About the Author: Cherie Dimaline is an internationally bestselling author. Her book The Marrow Thieves was named by Time magazine, one of the Best Ya Books of All Time and won the Governor General's Award and the Kirkus Prize. Her novel Empire of Wild was an instant Canadian bestseller and is being adapted into a full opera for the Canadian Opera Company. Hunting By Stars was a 2022 American Indian Library Association Honor Book and her novel Venco debuted at #1 on Canadian bestseller lists. Other titles include Funeral Songs for Dying Girls (Aila Honor Book, Aura Award winner, Crime Writers Best Book, Bram Stoker Finalist) and Into the Bright Open (2024 Governor General's Award Finalist). Cherie lives in her Georgian Bay Métis Community and has written and produced for Marvel, FX, HBO, Disney, and is currently adapting two major projects for AMC.
events.blurb: Hear Métis author Cherie Dimaline discuss her body of work and her novel Funeral Songs for Dying Girls.

events.title: Teen Halloween Roller Derby!
events.description: Join the Library for an afternoon of skating and crafting for teens at the Mitchell Park Bowl! This event will include free skating and equipment (roller skates, safety equipment) if needed, food, and a chance to win raffles prizes! Our program includes: Two skating sessions from 2-3:30 PM and 3:30-5 PM with Open Skate Spaces Free pizza and snacks throughout the three hour event, with Mister Softee Ice Cream from 2:30-4:30! Crafts Raffle prizes! A few things to keep in mind: When registering, please enter the attendee's name All attendees must fill out this waiver to skate with us! Costumes are welcome and encouraged, however please consider comfort and safety for roller skating Many thanks to the Community Services Department and the Friends of the Palo Alto Library for their support of this program and overall teen mental health and wellness in our community.
events.blurb: Skate and craft with fellow teens at Mitchell Park Bowl, with equipment and food on hand.

events.title: Halloween Storytime & Trick-or-Treat Parade (Ages 0-5)
events.description: Join us for a not-so-spooky Halloween celebration at the Library! Costumes are not required but encouraged at this Halloween-themed Storytime, which will take place outdoors on Civic Center Lawn. The fun continues afterwards in our Trick-or-Treat Parade, where we will circle around the Civic Center fountain. Library staff, Town staff, our friends from the New Museum of Los Gatos, LGS Recreation and the Friends Bookstore will have some goodies to pass out. Bring a bag or bucket for collecting goodies as you practice saying "trick or treat" (in words or in smiles!) See you there at the cutest event of the year!
events.blurb: Join an outdoor Halloween storytime on Civic Center Lawn, then march in the trick-or-treat parade.

events.title: Online Author Talk: E. Lockhart
events.description: Join us for an exciting author talk with #1 New York Times bestselling author E. Lockhart as we reflect on her impressive body of work, including the literary sensation We Were Liars, and even gain an exclusive sneak peek into her shimmering new thriller, The Pools. Once, in a small New England town known for its hot springs, something terrible happened. Something that should have been a warning to stay away from the pools, if the stories were to be believed. But no one is afraid of the water anymore, even if they should be. When new girl Lexie meets golden boy Chester, their chemistry is undeniable. She's running from a glittering life she won't speak about. He's hiding secrets of his own. Their connection feels bigger than both of them, despite their damage. One frigid winter morning in that small New England town, five people go for a swim in the pools. Five people, including Chester. What happens there sends shock waves through the town, changing life as Lexie knows it forever. Lockhart and ask questions live! About the Author: Lockhart is the #1 New York Times bestselling author of the Liars novels: We Were Liars, Family of Liars, and We Fell Apart. We Were Liars is also an original series on Prime Video. Her other books include Again Again, Genuine Fraud, and The Disreputable History of Frankie Landau-Banks. She has been a finalist for the Los Angeles Times Book Prize and the National Book Award and an honoree for the Printz Award. She lives in Brooklyn, New York.
events.blurb: Hear E. Lockhart discuss We Were Liars and get a preview of her new thriller, The Pools.

events.title: FOPAL Book Sale
events.description: Don't miss this month's Friends of the Palo Alto Library Book Sale! There will be three rooms with over 70,000 books, CDs, DVDs, puzzles, etc., new & gently used, all sorted, very reasonably priced! Proceeds benefit the Palo Alto libraries. For the safety and comfort of all participants, masks are suggested and room occupancy will be lower than usual. Please visit fopal.org for more information. Saturday Hours: Bargain Room 9:30 AM – 4 PM Children's Room 10 AM – 4 PM Main Room 11 AM – 4 PM Sunday Hours: All Rooms 1 PM – 4 PM
events.blurb: Browse three rooms of used books, CDs, DVDs, and puzzles at the Friends of the Palo Alto Library sale.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Paul Vigna
events.description: Join us for an eye-opening conversation with veteran journalist Paul Vigna as we examine his provocative book, The Almightier: How Money Became God, Greed Became Virtue, and Debt Became Sin, in which he explores the question: how did money go from a tool of commerce into the dominant faith of modern society? In The Almightier, Vigna takes readers on a sweeping historical journey from Renaissance Florence to today's global financial markets, revealing how wealth accumulation evolved from a moral failing into an unspoken civic virtue. He uncovers the forgotten history of money, tracing the uneasy and often accidental alliance between wealth and religion as it developed from ancient city-states to today's secular world, where religious devotion has receded and greed has stepped in to fill the void. Through engaging anecdotes, original research, and fresh perspectives on the causes of the many challenges we face today, Vigna makes a compelling argument that money has no power apart from the power we give it. Whether you are interested in economic history, personal finance, or the hidden cultural forces shaping modern life, this talk is sure to pique your interest. About the Author: Paul Vigna is an author, journalist, editor and speaker, with a particular focus on capital markets and cryptocurrencies. He is the author of Guts: The Anatomy of The Walking Dead and coauthor of The Age of Cryptocurrency and The Truth Machine. For 25 years, he was a reporter and editor for Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal, pioneering coverage of the cryptocurrency sector. He has appeared on CNN, Cnbc, Msnbc, Fox, and PBS.
events.blurb: Hear journalist Paul Vigna discuss how money evolved into a stand-in for morality and virtue.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Pyet Despain
events.description: Prepare your palate for a vibrant culinary journey with star chef Pyet De Spain, the inaugural winner of Gordon Ramsay's hit television competition Next Level Chef, as she presents her debut cookbook, Rooted in Fire: A Celebration of Native American and Mexican Cooking. Pyet De Spain rose to prominence as the first winner of Gordon Ramsey's Fox television show Next Level Chef. Now, in her debut cookbook, she shares the joy of cooking fueled by her burning passion for Native American and Mexican American cuisine. Pyet shows you how to incorporate a delicious range of key ingredients—from venison, dandelion greens, to sunchokes, bison, and native berries—into more than sixty fusion dishes. Family and friends will be excited to gather around the table to enjoy sweet and savory food such as: Three Sisters Salad Bison and Sweet Corn Soup Fry Bread Mexican Chocolate & Mezcal Cake Corn Silk and Honey Tea Wojapi BBQ Sauce Rooted in Fire is far more than just a collection of recipes; it is a movement giving voice to Indigenous culture, histories, and foodways through the universal language of food. Register for this event today and learn how to work with nature in your own kitchen. About the Author: Pyet—short for her inherited Native American name, Pyetwetmokwe—is a member of the Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation and an award-winning global private chef. She made history as the first winner of Gordon Ramsay's Next Level Chef and was named one of Entrepreneur Magazine's Top 25 Private Chefs in Los Angeles. Her work is centered on uplifting Indigenous foodways within the culinary industry while advocating for a more sustainable and sovereign food system for Indigenous peoples.
events.blurb: Hear chef Pyet De Spain talk through her debut cookbook of Native American and Mexican recipes.

events.title: Join-A-Ranger: Night Hike and Flashlight Tour
events.description: Enjoy a fun-filled Night Hike and Flashlight Tour of McClellan Ranch Preserve and Blackberry Farm! We will explore the woods and nature at night, learn about nocturnal animals' special adaptations, and test our heightened senses in the dark with games and activities. The hike is approximately one mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. Please wear appropriate walking shoes and a warm jacket and bring a flashlight or head-lamp. All attendees must register and children must be accompanied by an adult. $10 Resident | $13 Non-resident
events.blurb: Walk McClellan Ranch Preserve after dark with a ranger, learning how nocturnal animals adapt to nighttime.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Rebecca Roanhorse
events.description: Step into a sprawling world of celestial magic, political intrigue, and ancient prophecies with New York Times bestselling author Rebecca Roanhorse as we dive deep into her acclaimed Between Earth and Sky trilogy. Black Sun, Fevered Star, and Mirrored Heavens are inspired by the rich and diverse cultures of the pre-Columbian Americas, reshaping modern speculative fiction with unmissable worldbuilding. Black Sun, the first book in the trilogy, introduces us to the holy city of Tova. The winter solstice is usually a time for celebration and renewal, but this year it coincides with a solar eclipse, a rare celestial event proscribed by the Sun Priest as an unbalancing of the world. Meanwhile, a ship launches from a distant city bound for Tova and set to arrive on the solstice. The captain of the ship, Xiala, is a disgraced Teek whose song can calm the waters around her as easily as it can warp a man's mind. Her ship carries one passenger. Described as harmless, the passenger, Serapio, is a young man, blind, scarred, and cloaked in destiny. As Xiala well knows, when a man is described as harmless, he usually ends up being a villain. Whether you are a longtime fan of the trilogy or searching for your next immersive fantasy read, this is an event you won't want to miss out on. About the Author: Rebecca Roanhorse is a New York Times bestselling and Nebula, Hugo, and Locus Award-winning speculative fiction writer. She has published multiple award-winning short stories and novels, including two novels in The Sixth World series, Star Wars: Resistance Reborn, Race to the Sun for the Rick Riordan imprint, and the Hugo Award-winning epic fantasy trilogy Between Earth and Sky. She was the guest editor of America's Best Science Fiction and Fantasy (2023) and a contributor to the New York Times "100 Best Books of the 21st Century." She has also written for Marvel comics and games, and her TV writing includes FX's A Murder at the End of the World, and the Marvel series Echo for Disney+. She has had her own work optioned by Paramount, Amazon Studios, Netflix, and AMC Studios.
events.blurb: Discuss Rebecca Roanhorse's Between Earth and Sky trilogy with the New York Times bestselling author.

events.title: Festival of Lights: A Diwali Celebration
events.description: Join us at the Mitchell Park Community Center, as we celebrate Diwali! Enjoy fun activities for all ages including: Ongoing from 2-4 PM: Henna with teaching artist Rachel-Anne Palacios (Adobe Room; henna line closes at 3:30 PM!) Rangoli (chalk coloring craft outside in the Courtyard) Crafts (in Adobe Room) All activities available while supplies last! Performance from 2:30-3:30 PM in El Palo Alto Room by Noorani Dance. Rachel-Anne Palacios is an Afro-Chicana Oakland native, multi-cultural arts educator, and self-taught folk artist. She has been teaching art workshops and classes at Bay Area schools and libraries for over a decade and a half and her lessons and projects are inspired by indigenous cultures and traditional art from around the world. Noorani Dance, founded in 2016 by by international Kathak artist, Farah Yasmeen Shaikh, exemplifies Farah's unique artistic expression and vision coupled with the classical and innovative influence and style of Farah's Guru, the late Pandit Chitresh Das. "Noorani" means bright or luminous, with a dual meaning of enlightenment. With Kathak dance as their medium, Noorani Dance is committed to enlightening minds and hearts through the arts.
events.blurb: Get henna, try rangoli chalk art, and join other activities celebrating Diwali at Mitchell Park Community Center.

events.title: Deer Hollow Spooky Storytime
events.description: Together with our friends at Deer Hollow Farm, our librarians will present a spooky-themed storytime at the farm with books, songs, and rhymes. We will also get to meet some of the farm animals up close! Meet us there: Deer Hollow Farm, 22500 Cristo Rey Dr., Cupertino Please note: the parking lot for Deer Hollow Farm is about a one-mile flat, paved walk to the farm. We recommend walking shoes, hats, and/or strollers. Also, there will be limited seating-- prepare to sit on the floor if you can.
events.attendanceNote: Please note: the parking lot for Deer Hollow Farm is about a one-mile flat, paved walk to the farm. We recommend walking shoes, hats, and/or strollers. Also, there will be limited seating-- prepare to sit on the floor if you can.
events.blurb: Hear a spooky-themed storytime with books, songs, and rhymes, then meet farm animals up close.

events.title: Watershed Habitat of the Steelhead Nature Walk
events.description: Join a Naturalist and learn about the Steelhead life cycle, riparian habitat and challenges faced in Stevens Creek. We will walk through history and view our ecosystem through the lens of this phenomenal species. You and your child will identify aquatic insects as a measure of water quality. The hike is approximately one mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. All attendees must register and children must be accompanied by an adult. $25 Resident | $32 Non-resident
events.blurb: Walk along Stevens Creek with a naturalist to learn about the Steelhead life cycle and riparian habitat.

events.title: Demons, Creatures and Monsters - Oh My!
events.description: Registration is required. Meet the mythical creatures, legendary beasts, and terrifying monsters that have populated Asian art for centuries. Appearing throughout folklore, stories, songs, and works of art, these supernatural, mystical, and often godlike (or demonic) beings have fascinated audiences since ancient times. Presented by the Asian Art Museum. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Hear about the demons, creatures, and legendary beasts that populate centuries of Asian art and folklore.

events.title: Drop-in Bike Clinic
events.venue: Bike Fix-it Station (Outside Franklin St. Entrance)
events.description: Come join us every third Saturday of the month for the Drop-in Bike Clinic! Use our tools to work on your bike. All ages welcome. Professional bike mechanic Ryan Murphy will be available for advice and help with: Changing a tire Adjusting gears and brakes Identifying that mysterious noise, and more! Meet at our Dero Fix-it station, on Franklin Street. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Bring your bike and use the tools on hand while mechanic Ryan Murphy offers repair advice.

events.title: NUMU Youth Still Life: Spooky Skeleton Figure Drawing (Ages 7-16)
events.description: Meet us at the New Museum Los Gatos, where the staff will arrange a (fake decor) skeleton and a (decor) dog skeleton along with a few spooky objects from our collection for children ages 7-16 to sketch on black or gray paper with white drawing pencils. This event is a young artist's dream as it will take place in the Museum's professional studio setting! All materials are provided. Registration opens 3 weeks prior to the event.
events.blurb: Sketch a decorated skeleton and spooky museum objects in white pencil on dark paper at NUMU.

events.title: Join-A-Ranger: Bird ID and Guided Hike
events.description: The Park Rangers invite you to learn about the birds living in our riparian habitat and how to ID them! Walk the trails to see the environment they live in and maybe catch a glimpse of a Red-Shoulder Hawk, Screech Owl, or more! All attendees must register and an adult must accompany children. The hike is approximately one-quarter mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. $10 Resident | $13 Non-resident
events.blurb: Walk the trails with a Park Ranger to spot and identify local birds like hawks and owls.

events.title: Alice, Formerly of Wonderland
events.description: Seven-time Emmy Award-winning writer Mark Saltzman illuminates the beautiful coming-of-age story revealing the truth behind the fairy tale between Alice Liddell—the real-life inspiration of Lewis Carroll's classic tale—and Prince Leopold, Queen Victoria's youngest son. Brimming with wit and emotional spark, this a cappella musical weaves between Victorian reality and Wonderland whimsy, revealing a tender connection shaped by duty, distance, and the ache of what might have been. Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.
events.blurb: Watch the coming-of-age story of Alice Liddell and Prince Leopold unfold onstage at Lucie Stern Theatre.

Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.
events.blurb: Watch the coming-of-age story of Alice Liddell and Prince Leopold unfold onstage at Lucie Stern Theatre.

events.title: Shane
events.description: A Wild West classic. Honoring the original while cracking it wide open, Karen Zacarias' storytelling is a living, breathing world of the American frontier as told by voices too often left out of the legend. The play unfolds in the vast Wyoming prairies, where families fighting for their land are pushed to the breaking point by forces determined to drive them out. Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn't always about the fastest draw—it's about doing the right thing when it counts.
events.blurb: Watch a Wild West drama unfold on the Wyoming prairie, told through voices often left out of the legend.

events.title: Dracula
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Sink your teeth into the ultimate Halloween thrill. Steven Dietz's adaptation of the timeless classic seduces with elegance and suspense, turning the legendary vampire tale into a high-octane theatrical ride. Bold, chilling, and wickedly smart, the story draws you into a world where reason clashes with superstition and love becomes dangerously intoxicating. This Dracula keeps you leaning forward—never quite sure who holds the power, or what darkness waits just out of sight.
events.blurb: Watch this staged retelling of Dracula pull you into its shadowy, suspenseful world.
